note: operator: 'best practise, permanent resolution asap' — resolved without either option: root cause was ExpressVPN's WFP callout left running while disconnected, which dropped loopback traffic from browser-named processes into WSL mirrored mode; after the operator's ExpressVPN repair (2026-09-29 14:41) the service runs and browsers reach WSL (Edge headless ok on 127.0.0.1 and localhost:5051). Mirrored mode (D-360) stays.
question: How should browsers on Windows reach the WSL services again: through a relay on a different port, or by switching WSL back to NAT mode?
title: How should browsers on Windows reach the WSL services again: through a relay on a different port, or by switching WSL back to NAT mode?
